wc-walking-club-p2.title: Viết đoạn ngắn
wc-walking-club-p2.instr: Trả lời bằng câu hoàn chỉnh, 20–30 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 7 phút.
wc-walking-club-p2.body:
CÂU HỎI: When and where do you like walking?
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: I like walking in a nearby park on Sunday mornings. I enjoy it because the air is fresh. Also, it helps me reduce stress after a busy week.

wc-walking-club-p3.title: Trả lời nhóm chat
wc-walking-club-p3.instr: Trả lời các thành viên trong nhóm chat, mỗi câu 30–40 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 10 phút.
wc-walking-club-p3.body:
CÂU HỎI: I often go walking. Do you like walking?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! Yes, I really enjoy walking, especially in the evening. I like it because it helps me stay active and reduce stress. For example, I often walk around the lake near my house after work.

CÂU HỎI: I like walking, but when it rains, I get wet. Can you tell me about a bad experience you had while walking?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! One evening, while I was walking in the park, it suddenly started to rain heavily. I got completely wet because I did not bring an umbrella. As a result, I caught a bad cold the next day.

CÂU HỎI: Walking is one of the best types of exercise. What do you think when many people walk and know it is good for their health?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! Yes, I completely agree that walking is one of the best types of exercise. I think so because it is free and easy for everyone. I also believe it improves both our physical and mental health.

wc-walking-club-p4.title: Viết 2 email
wc-walking-club-p4.instr: Email cho bạn khoảng 50 từ (thân mật) và email cho quản lý 120–150 từ (trang trọng). Khoảng 30 phút.
wc-walking-club-p4.body:
CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend about the two-week European walking tour plan
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Miha,
I'm really excited about the idea of a European walking tour.
I think two weeks is too long because we're busy with university classes.
I'm considering suggesting a shorter domestic trip instead.
What do you think?
Talk soon,
Anh Hao

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club manager about the European walking tour plan
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about the two-week European walking tour. I am very excited that the club is planning a trip abroad, but I have some concerns about this plan.
I would like to suggest organising a shorter trip instead. I believe this would suit more members because many of us are busy with work and university classes and cannot take two weeks off. However, a trip to Europe is also very expensive for students on a tight budget.
If a short trip abroad is not possible, we could organise a two-day weekend walk in a nearby province. I also suggest planning the European tour for next year, so that members have enough time to save money and arrange their holidays.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Anh Hao

CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend about members using phones while walking (safety issue)
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Tu,
I'm really worried about members using their phones during our walks.
I think it's extremely dangerous because they don't notice the traffic.
I'm considering suggesting a strict rule to keep everyone safe.
What do you think?
Talk soon,
Anh Hao

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club manager about members using phones while walking (safety issue)
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about members using their phones during our walks. I am very concerned about this habit, as it is extremely dangerous on busy roads.
I would like to suggest creating a clear club rule that phones may only be used during rest breaks. I believe this rule would work because walkers who look at their screens often fail to notice cars, bicycles and uneven paths. However, some members may need their phones for maps or emergencies.
If a strict rule is not possible, we could ask one leader in each group to carry a phone for maps and emergencies. I also suggest giving a short safety talk before each walk, so that everyone remembers to stay alert.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Anh Hao

sp4n-01.title: 1. A time you worked hard to achieve your goal
sp4n-01.instr: Kể về lần đạt thành tựu. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-01.body:
CÂU HỎI: A time you worked hard to achieve your goal.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I worked really hard to achieve my goal.
A few months ago, I had an important goal at work. I needed to complete a difficult IT task while I was also studying at university.
At first, it was quite difficult because I had a lot of work to do. I had to manage my time carefully. I usually worked during the day and studied in the evening.
I spent a lot of time learning new things, checking technical documents and discussing problems with my colleagues.
Finally, I completed the task successfully and I was very happy with the result.
**It taught me that hard work and good time management are very important if we want to achieve our goals.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel when you achieved your goal?
BÀI MẪU: I felt really happy and proud of myself. I was also relieved because I had spent a lot of time and effort on it.
More importantly, I became more confident because I realized that I could deal with difficult situations if I didn't give up.
CÂU HỎI: How should people be encouraged to achieve their goals?
BÀI MẪU: In my opinion, people should be encouraged by setting realistic goals and getting support from others.
For example, at work, managers can give employees useful feedback and recognize their achievements.
I also think people should focus on their progress instead of comparing themselves with others.
**If people feel supported and see their own progress, they will be more motivated to achieve their goals.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: goal | difficult | manage time | work hard | complete | successful | proud | confident

sp4n-02.title: 2. A time you faced a challenge
sp4n-02.instr: Kể lần đối mặt thử thách. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-02.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you faced a challenge.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a challenge I faced at work.
A few months ago, I had to solve a technical problem on a server. The system was not working properly, and it affected some users.
At first, I felt quite worried because I didn't know exactly what caused the problem.
However, I didn't give up. I checked the system logs, searched for information and discussed the problem with my colleagues.
After trying several solutions, we finally found the cause and fixed the problem.
**It was a difficult experience, but I learned a lot from it.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel about that experience?
BÀI MẪU: At first, I felt worried and stressed because it was an important problem.
However, after solving it, I felt very happy and proud of myself.
I also became more confident because I learned how to deal with technical problems more effectively.
CÂU HỎI: Do you think people need challenges in life? Why or why not?
BÀI MẪU: Yes, definitely. I think challenges are an important part of life.
First, they help us learn new things and improve our skills.
Second, challenges can make us stronger and more confident.
For example, when I have a difficult problem at work, I have to think carefully and find a solution.
**So, I believe challenges are necessary for personal and professional development.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: challenge | problem | worried | logs | colleagues | solution | fix | confident

sp4n-03.title: 3. A time you were in a hurry
sp4n-03.instr: Kể lần vội vàng, bận rộn; nêu quan điểm về cuộc sống hiện đại bận rộn. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-03.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me a time when you were in a hurry.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a time when I was in a hurry.
It happened a few months ago. I had an important meeting at work in the morning, but I woke up late.
I quickly got dressed, had a simple breakfast and went to work as fast as possible.
Unfortunately, there was a lot of traffic on the road, so I was quite worried about being late.
Luckily, I arrived just a few minutes before the meeting started.
**Since then, I have tried to prepare everything the night before and wake up earlier.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel?
BÀI MẪU: I felt very stressed and worried because I didn't want to be late for the meeting.
I also realized that rushing can make people forget important things.
After that experience, I learned that good preparation can save a lot of time.
CÂU HỎI: Modern life makes us busier and more rushed. What do you think?
BÀI MẪU: Yes, I agree with this idea.
Nowadays, people have many responsibilities. They have to work, study, take care of their families and deal with many messages and emails.
Technology makes our lives more convenient, but sometimes it also makes us feel that we always have to be available.
**I think people should manage their time carefully and make time for rest.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: wake up late | meeting | traffic | stressed | preparation | responsibilities | technology | rest

sp4n-04.title: 4. A time you learned something new
sp4n-04.instr: Kể lần học kỹ năng mới. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-04.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time you learned something new.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I learned a new IT skill.
Last year, I started learning about OpenShift because it was useful for my work.
At first, I found it quite difficult because there were many new concepts and technical terms.
I watched online tutorials, read documents and practiced on my own.
Sometimes I made mistakes, but I tried to understand why they happened.
After several weeks, I became more familiar with the technology and I could use some of it at work.
**I felt really happy because I learned something useful for my career.**
CÂU HỎI: What do you think about the belief that older people don't learn anything new?
BÀI MẪU: I don't agree with this belief.
I think people can learn new things at any age.
Older people may learn more slowly than young people in some situations, but they have more life experience and knowledge.
If they are interested and have enough time, they can learn new skills successfully.
CÂU HỎI: It's never too late to start learning a new skill. What are your thoughts?
BÀI MẪU: I completely agree.
Learning is a lifelong process, so people should not stop learning when they become older.
For example, older people can learn how to use smartphones, computers or online services.
Learning new skills can also help people stay active and confident.
**In my opinion, the most important thing is not age but motivation and willingness to learn.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: new skill | OpenShift | difficult | tutorials | practice | mistakes | career | lifelong learning

sp4n-05.title: 5. Travel / an adventure in nature
sp4n-05.instr: Kể lần du lịch, khám phá thiên nhiên. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-05.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about somewhere you have traveled / an adventure in nature.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a trip I took with some friends.
Last summer, we traveled to a mountainous area in Vietnam.
The journey took several hours, but the scenery was beautiful. We saw green mountains, small villages and beautiful rice fields.
We also went hiking and spent time taking photos and talking together.
It was different from my normal life in the city because it was much quieter and more peaceful.
**It was one of the most memorable trips I've ever had.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel?
BÀI MẪU: I felt very relaxed and excited during the trip.
I especially enjoyed being close to nature because my daily life is usually quite busy.
I also felt closer to my friends because we had more time to talk and share experiences.
CÂU HỎI: What is the importance of understanding the customs where you travel?
BÀI MẪU: I think understanding local customs is very important.
First, it shows respect for local people and their culture.
Second, it helps travelers avoid misunderstandings.
For example, different places may have different rules about food, clothes or communication.
**If we understand local customs, we can have a more enjoyable and respectful trip.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: trip | mountains | scenery | hiking | peaceful | relaxed | culture | respect

sp4n-06.title: 6. Received a gift / read a good book
sp4n-06.instr: Kể về lần nhận quà hoặc đọc sách. Nên chọn kể về món quà vì dễ nói hơn. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-06.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me a time you received a gift from someone.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a gift I received from one of my close friends.
It was my birthday a few years ago. My friend gave me a simple watch.
It wasn't very expensive, but I really liked it because my friend chose it especially for me.
I still remember that day because we had dinner together and talked about our work and life.
I have used the watch for a long time, so it has become quite meaningful to me.
**For me, the meaning of a gift is more important than its price.**
CÂU HỎI: How do you feel when you receive a gift?
BÀI MẪU: I usually feel happy and appreciated when I receive a gift.
I don't really care about the price.
What matters to me is the thought and effort behind the gift.
It makes me feel that the other person cares about me.
CÂU HỎI: A handmade present is better than a present bought from a shop. What do you think?
BÀI MẪU: I partly agree with this idea.
A handmade gift can be more personal because the person has spent time and effort making it.
However, a gift bought from a shop can also be meaningful if we choose it carefully.
For example, we can choose something that matches the person's interests.
**So, I think the meaning of a gift is more important than whether it is handmade or store-bought.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: birthday | friend | watch | simple | meaningful | appreciate | handmade | personal

sp4n-07.title: 7. A time you received good news
sp4n-07.instr: Kể về lần nhận tin tốt. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-07.body:
CÂU HỎI: Describe a time you received good news.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I received some good news.
A few months ago, I received good news about my work.
My manager told me that I had successfully completed an important task.
I had spent a lot of time working on it, so I was really happy when I heard the news.
I immediately told my family and some of my close friends.
**It gave me more motivation to work harder and improve my skills.**
CÂU HỎI: What do you think about information being easily accessible through various channels?
BÀI MẪU: I think it is very useful.
Nowadays, we can get information quickly through websites, social media, email and mobile applications.
This saves us a lot of time and helps us make decisions more easily.
However, not all information online is reliable, so we need to be careful.
CÂU HỎI: People receive a vast amount of information daily. What should they pay attention to?
BÀI MẪU: In my opinion, people should pay attention to the source and reliability of information.
They shouldn't believe everything they see on social media.
Before sharing important information, they should check it on reliable websites or from official sources.
**I think being able to identify reliable information is an important skill in modern life.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: good news | work | successful | happy | motivation | information | reliable | official source

sp4n-08.title: 8. Extreme sport
sp4n-08.instr: Kể lần chơi hoặc xem người khác chơi thể thao mạo hiểm; nêu quan điểm có nên cho trẻ em chơi không. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-08.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell a time you did or saw someone do an extreme sport.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a time when I tried an adventurous activity with my friends.
It happened during a trip. We decided to go hiking on a fairly difficult mountain trail.
The trail was quite steep in some places, so we had to be very careful.
At first, I was a little scared because I wasn't used to this kind of activity.
However, my friends encouraged me, and I continued.
When we reached the top, I felt extremely happy and excited.
**It was challenging but also a very memorable experience.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel?
BÀI MẪU: At first, I felt nervous because the activity was quite difficult.
But after I got used to it, I started to enjoy the experience.
When I reached the top, I felt proud because I had overcome my fear.
CÂU HỎI: Should adults allow children to play extreme sports?
BÀI MẪU: I think it depends on the type of sport and the age of the child.
Extreme sports can help children become more confident and physically active.
However, safety should always come first.
Adults should choose suitable activities and make sure children have proper equipment and supervision.
**So, I don't think children should be completely prevented from trying adventurous activities, but they need to be carefully controlled.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: adventure | hiking | difficult | steep | nervous | overcome fear | safety | supervision

sp4n-09.title: 9. Worked in a team
sp4n-09.instr: Kể về lần làm việc nhóm. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-09.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you worked in a team.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I worked in a team at my company.
Last year, my team had to complete an important IT project.
There were several people in the team, and each person had a different responsibility.
My main responsibility was related to the technical part of the project.
We had regular meetings to discuss our progress and solve problems.
Sometimes we had different opinions, but we listened to each other and tried to find the best solution.
Finally, we completed the project successfully and on time.
**It was a very useful experience for me.**
CÂU HỎI: How do you feel when you work in a team?
BÀI MẪU: I generally enjoy working in a team.
I feel that teamwork gives me an opportunity to learn from other people.
It also makes difficult tasks easier because we can share responsibilities.
However, good communication is very important because everyone needs to understand their role.
CÂU HỎI: What are the advantages of teamwork?
BÀI MẪU: There are several advantages of teamwork.
First, people can share their knowledge and experience.
Second, teamwork allows people to divide a large task into smaller tasks.
It can also help people find better solutions because they have different ideas.
For example, in IT projects, developers, testers and system engineers can work together to solve technical problems.
**Therefore, I believe teamwork is very important in the modern workplace.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: team | project | responsibility | meeting | communication | different opinions | share | solution

sp4n-10.title: 10. A sports event
sp4n-10.instr: Kể lần xem sự kiện thể thao. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-10.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you went to a sports event.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a sports event I went to with my friends.
A few years ago, we went to a football match in my city.
There were many people at the stadium, and the atmosphere was amazing.
Before the match started, people were singing and supporting their favorite team.
The match was very exciting because the score was quite close.
When our team scored a goal, everyone shouted and celebrated together.
**It was a really enjoyable and unforgettable experience.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel during that event?
BÀI MẪU: I felt very excited and energetic.
I enjoyed watching the match, but I also enjoyed the atmosphere in the stadium.
It was interesting to see so many people sharing the same interest.
I forgot about my work and daily problems for a few hours.
CÂU HỎI: Do you think sports events are important for people?
BÀI MẪU: Yes, I think sports events are important for several reasons.
First, they encourage people to be more physically active.
Second, they bring people together and create a sense of community.
Sports events can also help people reduce stress after work or study.
**For example, watching a football match with friends can be a great way to relax and build relationships.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: football | stadium | atmosphere | exciting | score | celebrate | community | reduce stress

sp4n-11.title: 11. A time you helped someone
sp4n-11.instr: Kể lần giúp ai đó. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-11.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you helped someone.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I helped a new colleague at my company. A few months ago, he joined our team and struggled with setting up a server. He felt very stressed because the deadline was near. So, I decided to help him. We checked the system together and fixed the error step by step. Finally, he completed his task on time, and he was very happy.
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel about helping that person?
BÀI MẪU: I felt really happy and proud of myself. Helping him also helped me review my own knowledge and improve my teamwork skills. More importantly, it helped us build a good working relationship and trust each other more.
CÂU HỎI: Do you think helping others is important in the workplace? Why or why not?
BÀI MẪU: Yes, absolutely. In my opinion, helping others creates a friendly working environment. When people support each other, work can be done much faster and better. Moreover, a supportive team makes everyone feel more comfortable and motivated at work.
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: new colleague | system error | help step by step | proud | teamwork | good environment

sp4n-12.title: 12. A time you changed yourself
sp4n-12.instr: Kể lần thay đổi bản thân. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
sp4n-12.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you changed yourself.
BÀI MẪU: Well, I'd like to talk about a time when I decided to improve my time management skills. In the past, I used to wake up late and do things without a plan. Because of that, I was often stressed with my work and study. So, I decided to change my habits. I started waking up earlier, making a daily to-do list, and spending less time on social media. After a few weeks, my life became much more organized.
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel after making this change?
BÀI MẪU: At first, it was quite difficult to change my old habits. However, after seeing the good results, I felt very happy and confident. I realized that self-discipline helps me work better and save a lot of time.
CÂU HỎI: Why is changing oneself or personal development important for people?
BÀI MẪU: I believe changing oneself is very important for everyone. Life is always changing, so if we don't improve ourselves, we will stay behind. Learning new skills or changing bad habits helps us become stronger, more confident, and ready for new challenges in life.
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: time management | bad habit | wake up early | to-do list | organized | confident | personal development

sp1-01.title: Bộ 1
sp1-01.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-01.body:
CÂU HỎI: What did you do last night? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Last night was a balanced mix of productivity and relaxation. Right after a quick dinner with my family, I immediately got down to business, dedicating a good couple of hours to tackling my assignments and meticulously reviewing my notes for the upcoming exam. Once those academic duties were wrapped up, I needed to unwind. I spent about thirty minutes listening to music and watching a short film to switch off. Finally, I had a quick catch-up with my friends online and was out like a light by 11:30p.m. It was a very satisfying end to the day, all in all.
CÂU HỎI: What did you do on the weekend? | 30
BÀI MẪU: My last weekend was quite invigorating. On Saturday, I decided to make the most of the good weather, so I went hiking with my friends at a nearby nature reserve—it was a great way to recharge my batteries and switch off. Then, on Sunday, I had a more laid-back day. I spent the morning immersed in a novel, and in the afternoon, I paid a visit to my grandparents. We enjoyed some truly quality time together. I felt completely rejuvenated by the end of it.
CÂU HỎI: What do you like doing in your free time? | 30
BÀI MẪU: When I get some downtime, I primarily turn to music for relaxation, and specifically, I'm a big fan of country music. I find it incredibly soothing and comforting. After a demanding day of work or study, immersing myself in those mellow tunes is the perfect way to unwind and clear my head. It genuinely helps me switch off from my responsibilities and ensures I feel completely refreshed and ready for the next day.

sp1-02.title: Bộ 2
sp1-02.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-02.body:
CÂU HỎI: What do you like doing with your friends? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I always prioritise spending my downtime with my friends; it's essential for me. While we enjoy a lot of activities - like catching a film or hitting a concert occasionally - I'm particularly keen on simply hanging out at a local coffee shop. We usually grab some great drinks, like green tea or a good espresso, and it’s the perfect setting to catch up on exciting news and share anecdotes. It’s just great quality time and it helps me recharge my batteries socially.
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about one of your good memories | 30
BÀI MẪU: One memory that stands out vividly for me is the day I successfully completed my first major marathon. It was a huge personal challenge. I remember the incredible feeling of elation and relief crossing the finish line, especially since I had been training rigorously for months. The cheering crowds and the sight of my family waiting there made the whole experience absolutely unforgettable. It truly taught me the value of perseverance.
CÂU HỎI: What is the weather like today? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Well, the weather in Hanoi today is absolutely delightful - it’s quintessential autumn. It’s pleasantly cool, with the temperature hovering around 18 to 20 degrees Celsius. The sky is largely clear, but there’s a slight, gentle breeze which makes it feel a bit crisp. This is my favourite kind of weather, actually, as it’s perfect for taking a leisurely walk outside without feeling too cold. All in all, it’s a beautifully mild day.

sp1-03.title: Bộ 3
sp1-03.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-03.body:
CÂU HỎI: What is your favorite season? | 30
BÀI MẪU: My absolute favourite season is definitely autumn. I just find the atmosphere incredibly inviting and serene. I particularly appreciate the pleasant shift in weather; it’s neither oppressively hot nor bitterly cold - just pleasantly crisp. I love watching the leaves turn those gorgeous shades of red and gold. Moreover, the air quality is much better, which makes it perfect for taking leisurely strolls. Ultimately, autumn provides the perfect backdrop for relaxation and reflection.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about your friend? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I'd love to talk about Mai, who is easily my closest friend. We actually met while studying the same degree at university, and we've been inseparable ever since. We often collaborate on assignments together, usually hitting the library after class to knuckle down on our homework. What I value most, though, is how she's my confidante—we share everything and constantly support each other. She’s genuinely a fantastic companion.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a member in your family? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I’d love to talk about my mother, who has played a truly essential role in my life. She’s currently 51 and possesses a wonderful sense of humour; she's genuinely both a great mother and my closest friend. What I value most is her wisdom - she always offers invaluable advice whenever I face a difficult dilemma. Her unwavering support and understanding have been absolutely fundamental to my personal development. I admire her immensely.

sp1-04.title: Bộ 4
sp1-04.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-04.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me the best way to travel around your country? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Without a doubt, I'd argue that the motorbike is the optimal way to navigate Vietnam. While buses are certainly cost-effective, they are far less comfortable and prone to traffic congestion during peak hours, especially in major hubs like Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City. Motorbikes, in contrast, offer unrivalled convenience and, crucially, absolute freedom. They allow you to access narrow alleys and stop whenever you want, making them the best option for truly exploring the country.
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about a famous place in your country? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Although my home province of Vinh Phuc has many scenic spots, I believe Tam Dao is the most renowned. Located just 30 kilometers from the city center, it serves as a fantastic escape. It's primarily known for its exceptionally fresh air and picturesque mountain scenery. At the weekend, it’s the perfect getaway for families or friends to recharge and enjoy outdoor activities like throwing a barbecue. I highly recommend everyone visit this beautiful, serene destination at least once.
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about yourself? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Certainly. My name is Anna Mai, and I'm currently a senior student specializing in Accounting at the National Economics University. I would describe myself as very sociable and easy-going. Outside of my studies, I prioritize spending time with friends - we enjoy hanging out, often catching a film or simply grabbing a bite to eat. Looking ahead, I aspire
to become a certified auditor, as I believe it offers a solid foundation in finance while simultaneously enhancing my soft skills.

sp1-05.title: Bộ 5
sp1-05.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-05.body:
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about your family? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I live in a nuclear family with my parents and my older brother. My father is a dedicated farmer in the countryside, whereas my mother is a full-time homemaker. My brother, who is a qualified engineer, and I both work as office professionals in the city. Consequently, we only manage to reunite during major national holidays, such as Tết or National Day. Despite the distance, we remain extremely close-knit and cherish those precious gatherings.
CÂU HỎI: Describe your favorite places? | 30
BÀI MẪU: While there are many places I enjoy, Nha Trang is undoubtedly my top destination. I genuinely believe it's one of the most stunning coastal cities in Vietnam, thanks to its pristine beaches and clear water. I always look forward to spending an extended break there because it offers the perfect opportunity to unwind completely, indulge in fresh seafood, and partake in various water sports. Ultimately, Nha Trang is the ideal spot to recharge and find new inspiration.
CÂU HỎI: What do you like to do in your free time? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I have always considered myself an avid movie enthusiast, so naturally, my favourite way to spend my downtime is binge-watching different series on platforms like Netflix. I find it the perfect activity to unwind completely after a demanding schedule. For me, getting immersed in a compelling storyline is not just entertainment; it’s genuinely the most effective way to switch off from reality and recharge my batteries both mentally and emotionally.

sp1-06.title: Bộ 6
sp1-06.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-06.body:
CÂU HỎI: Describe your typical day? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Although I’m not naturally an early bird, I try to start my day early. I usually begin with a 30-minute workout, go to the office at 8 a.m., and finish work around 5 p.m. I aim to conclude my day around 11 p.m. by simply putting my mind at ease. Crucially, this schedule isn’t entirely fixed; it remains flexible and often depends heavily on my workload and professional commitments.
CÂU HỎI: Describe a typical Vietnamese meal? | 30
BÀI MẪU: A typical Vietnamese meal is centered around a bowl of rice, complemented by a main protein dish - usually meat or fish - and a variety of freshly sourced vegetables. While our meals are diverse, the iconic dish is undeniably Phở - a fragrant rice noodle soup served with either beef or chicken. Crucially, Vietnamese cuisine adheres to the Yin and Yang balance, ensuring ingredients like 'cold' balut are always paired with 'hot' elements such as ginger, creating a harmonious and nutritious experience.
CÂU HỎI: When do you feel tired? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I generally feel the most exhausted right before Tết, our Lunar New Year. That period involves a multitude of tasks, such as meticulously decorating, cleaning the house, and gathering necessary items. Furthermore, since the entire family gathers for this vital function, I’m responsible for welcoming guests and ensuring everyone is well-fed. Consequently, I feel completely drained. However, the immense joy of celebrating our tradition and the precious opportunity

sp1-07.title: Bộ 7
sp1-07.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-07.body:
CÂU HỎI: What are you wearing today? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Since today is typical of Hanoi's crisp autumn weather, I've opted for a comfortable yet stylish ensemble. I'm wearing a dress, which I’ve paired with a lightweight jacket to combat the slight chill. To complete the look, I added a hat as an accessory and some practical shoes. Essentially, my outfit is designed for both comfort and elegance, making it perfectly suited for the mild autumn climate.
CÂU HỎI: Describe your journey here today? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I'm thrilled to talk about my journey here\! I got up bright and early at 6 a.m. to prepare, and then drove to pick up my friend so we could do some last-minute revision together. We had to set off early because we live in a small town about 50 kilometers away. Consequently, we rode a motorbike under the hot summer sun to reach the British Council Centre. Despite having butterflies in our stomachs, we are determined to pass the exam with flying colors.
CÂU HỎI: Describe the room you are in? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Frankly, I'm currently in a fairly spacious examination room, roughly 40 square meters, with distinctive white and mallard green walls. The room is well-equipped with 50 computer desks and climate control provided by both fans and air conditioners. While there are three supervisors ensuring everything runs smoothly, the overall atmosphere is undeniably stressful. However, despite feeling nervous, I'm focused on doing my absolute best to pass the exam with flying colors.

sp1-08.title: Bộ 8
sp1-08.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-08.body:
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about your first school? | 30
BÀI MẪU: My first school was Ngo Gia Tu Primary School, located right in the middle of my hometown in the countryside. I remember it vividly because it was my dream school; it looked incredibly beautiful. All the walls were painted in multiple bright colours, which made it truly stand out from the surrounding buildings. Conveniently, it only took me about ten minutes to stroll there every single day. It holds many fond memories for me.
CÂU HỎI: Favorite book in your country? | 30
BÀI MẪU: While there are countless great works in Vietnamese literature, my favourite is undeniably The Tale of Kiều. It's an iconic 19th-century epic poem that I believe every Vietnamese person should read. The language is incredibly beautiful and the story is profoundly moving. It explores timeless themes like fate and perseverance through adversity. Reading it always gives me a deeper appreciation for our culture and history, which is why it stands out as the most cherished work.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me why you are interested in travel. | 30
BÀI MẪU: My interest in travel stems from its power to rejuvenate and inspire me. It’s the ultimate way to switch off from my daily stress and work pressure. When I travel, I get the chance to immerse myself in new cultures, explore breathtaking landscapes, and indulge in local cuisine. Meeting new people and seeing different perspectives genuinely helps broaden my horizons. Ultimately, travel doesn't just relax me; it provides the necessary vitality to tackle new challenges.

sp1-09.title: Bộ 9
sp1-09.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-09.body:
CÂU HỎI: When do you feel stressed? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I primarily feel stressed when I'm under intense work pressure or facing multiple tight deadlines simultaneously. Additionally, struggling to find the right English vocabulary when speaking can be quite frustrating. To manage this, I consciously make an effort to take a recharge break - either by immersing myself in some soothing music or by taking a quick stroll outside. This usually helps me clear my head and regain my focus.
CÂU HỎI: What is the food like in your country? | 30
BÀI MẪU: To describe Vietnamese cuisine in one word, I'd say it's excellent. Although the dishes may look simple, they are prepared in a very elaborate way, beautifully decorated, and offer a rich flavour profile with an incredible aroma. Crucially, our cooking always aims to balance the Yin and Yang elements, making the food both nourishing and healthy. Furthermore, the ingredients are always readily available, cheap, and exceptionally fresh, which is why I love Vietnamese food so much.
CÂU HỎI: Describe your job? | 30
BÀI MẪU: My current role is a salesman for a high-end fashion brand in a busy city centre location, and I genuinely love it. This position demands exceptional communication skills to truly persuade clients of the product's value, and crucially, a highly-developed art of observation to subtly anticipate their needs. What I find most appealing is the opportunity to interact with diverse people and, fundamentally, to make customers feel truly delighted with their luxury purchase. It's rewarding to share the product's intrinsic value.

sp1-10.title: Bộ 10
sp1-10.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
sp1-10.body:
CÂU HỎI: Which sports do people like in your country? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Well, football is undoubtedly the most popular sport in Vietnam. You can easily find people of all ages playing on local football pitches every afternoon. Besides that, sports like badminton, basketball, and running are also gaining a lot of traction because people are becoming more health-conscious nowadays.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me the last time you went to the movies? | 30
BÀI MẪU: The last time I went to the movies was about two weeks ago. I went to a cinema near my house with two close friends on a Saturday evening. We watched an action film that had just come out, and it was really exciting, with amazing special effects and a great soundtrack. Before the film, we bought popcorn and soft drinks, and afterwards we went out for dinner and talked about our favourite scenes. It was a fun and relaxing way to end a busy week.

v-sp-relax.title: Speaking: Thư giãn & giải trí
v-sp-relax.body:
unwind | /ʌnˈwaɪnd/ | thư giãn, xả hơi | After a long day, music helps me unwind. | Sau một ngày dài, âm nhạc giúp tôi thư giãn.
switch off | /swɪtʃ ˈɒf/ | gác lại mọi lo nghĩ, xả đầu óc | Watching a short film helps me switch off. | Xem một bộ phim ngắn giúp tôi xả đầu óc.
recharge my batteries | /ˌriːˈtʃɑːdʒ maɪ ˈbætəriz/ | nạp lại năng lượng | Hiking is a great way to recharge my batteries. | Leo núi là cách tuyệt vời để nạp lại năng lượng.
downtime | /ˈdaʊntaɪm/ | thời gian rảnh, nghỉ ngơi | I spend my downtime with my friends. | Tôi dành thời gian rảnh với bạn bè.
laid-back | /ˌleɪdˈbæk/ | thong thả, thư thái | On Sunday, I had a more laid-back day. | Chủ nhật tôi có một ngày thong thả hơn.
rejuvenated | /rɪˈdʒuːvəneɪtɪd/ | tràn đầy sức sống trở lại | I felt completely rejuvenated by the end of the weekend. | Cuối tuần đó tôi thấy tràn đầy sức sống trở lại.
invigorating | /ɪnˈvɪɡəreɪtɪŋ/ | tiếp thêm sinh lực, sảng khoái | My last weekend was quite invigorating. | Cuối tuần vừa rồi của tôi khá sảng khoái.
soothing | /ˈsuːðɪŋ/ | êm dịu, làm dịu | I find country music incredibly soothing. | Tôi thấy nhạc đồng quê rất êm dịu.
immerse myself in | /ɪˈmɜːs maɪˈself ɪn/ | đắm mình vào | I love to immerse myself in a good novel. | Tôi thích đắm mình vào một cuốn tiểu thuyết hay.
quality time | /ˈkwɒləti taɪm/ | khoảng thời gian ý nghĩa bên nhau | We enjoyed some quality time together. | Chúng tôi có khoảng thời gian thật ý nghĩa bên nhau.
binge-watch | /ˈbɪndʒ wɒtʃ/ | xem liền nhiều tập phim | I like binge-watching series on Netflix. | Tôi thích cày phim bộ trên Netflix.
avid | /ˈævɪd/ | say mê, cuồng nhiệt | I'm an avid movie enthusiast. | Tôi là người rất mê phim.
catch up on | /kætʃ ˈʌp ɒn/ | cập nhật, kể cho nhau nghe (tin tức) | We meet at a coffee shop to catch up on exciting news. | Chúng tôi gặp ở quán cà phê để kể nhau nghe tin mới.
hang out | /hæŋ ˈaʊt/ | đi chơi, tụ tập | I enjoy hanging out at a local coffee shop. | Tôi thích tụ tập ở quán cà phê gần nhà.
leisurely stroll | /ˈleʒəli strəʊl/ | cuộc đi dạo thong thả | Autumn is perfect for taking leisurely strolls. | Mùa thu rất hợp để đi dạo thong thả.
out like a light | /aʊt laɪk ə laɪt/ | ngủ say ngay lập tức | I was out like a light by 11:30 p.m. | Tôi ngủ say từ 11 giờ 30.

v-sp-place.title: Speaking: Thời tiết, nơi chốn & du lịch
v-sp-place.body:
crisp | /krɪsp/ | (thời tiết) se lạnh, trong lành | The air feels cool and crisp in autumn. | Mùa thu không khí mát và se lạnh.
breeze | /briːz/ | làn gió nhẹ | There's a slight, gentle breeze today. | Hôm nay có làn gió nhẹ.
mild | /maɪld/ | ôn hòa, dễ chịu | It's a beautifully mild day. | Hôm nay là một ngày ôn hòa, dễ chịu.
quintessential | /ˌkwɪntɪˈsenʃl/ | điển hình, tiêu biểu nhất | Today's weather is quintessential autumn. | Thời tiết hôm nay là mùa thu điển hình.
serene | /səˈriːn/ | thanh bình, yên tĩnh | Tam Dao is a beautiful, serene destination. | Tam Đảo là điểm đến đẹp và thanh bình.
picturesque | /ˌpɪktʃəˈresk/ | đẹp như tranh | It's known for its picturesque mountain scenery. | Nơi đây nổi tiếng với cảnh núi đẹp như tranh.
pristine | /ˈprɪstiːn/ | hoang sơ, sạch đẹp nguyên vẹn | Nha Trang has pristine beaches and clear water. | Nha Trang có bãi biển hoang sơ và nước trong.
renowned | /rɪˈnaʊnd/ | nổi tiếng | Tam Dao is the most renowned place in my province. | Tam Đảo là nơi nổi tiếng nhất tỉnh tôi.
getaway | /ˈɡetəweɪ/ | chốn nghỉ ngắn ngày | It's the perfect weekend getaway for families. | Đó là chốn nghỉ cuối tuần lý tưởng cho gia đình.
breathtaking | /ˈbreθteɪkɪŋ/ | đẹp ngoạn mục | I love exploring breathtaking landscapes. | Tôi thích khám phá những cảnh quan ngoạn mục.
broaden my horizons | /ˈbrɔːdn maɪ həˈraɪznz/ | mở mang tầm nhìn | Meeting new people helps broaden my horizons. | Gặp gỡ người mới giúp tôi mở mang tầm nhìn.
indulge in | /ɪnˈdʌldʒ ɪn/ | tận hưởng, thưởng thức thỏa thích | In Nha Trang, I indulge in fresh seafood. | Ở Nha Trang tôi thưởng thức hải sản tươi thỏa thích.
cost-effective | /ˌkɒst ɪˈfektɪv/ | tiết kiệm chi phí | Buses are cost-effective but less comfortable. | Xe buýt tiết kiệm nhưng kém thoải mái hơn.
traffic congestion | /ˈtræfɪk kənˈdʒestʃən/ | ùn tắc giao thông | Buses are prone to traffic congestion. | Xe buýt dễ bị kẹt xe.
peak hours | /piːk ˈaʊəz/ | giờ cao điểm | The roads are very crowded during peak hours. | Đường rất đông vào giờ cao điểm.
cuisine | /kwɪˈziːn/ | ẩm thực | Vietnamese cuisine balances Yin and Yang. | Ẩm thực Việt Nam cân bằng âm dương.

v-sp-people.title: Speaking: Con người, cảm xúc & công việc
v-sp-people.body:
confidante | /ˈkɒnfɪdænt/ | người bạn tâm giao | She's my confidante; we share everything. | Cô ấy là bạn tâm giao, chúng tôi chia sẻ mọi điều.
inseparable | /ɪnˈseprəbl/ | thân thiết không rời | We've been inseparable ever since. | Từ đó chúng tôi luôn gắn bó không rời.
close-knit | /ˌkləʊs ˈnɪt/ | gắn bó khăng khít | We remain an extremely close-knit family. | Gia đình tôi vẫn rất gắn bó.
nuclear family | /ˌnjuːkliə ˈfæməli/ | gia đình hạt nhân (bố mẹ và con) | I live in a nuclear family with my parents and my brother. | Tôi sống trong gia đình hạt nhân với bố mẹ và anh trai.
invaluable advice | /ɪnˈvæljuəbl ədˈvaɪs/ | lời khuyên vô giá | My mother always offers invaluable advice. | Mẹ luôn cho tôi những lời khuyên vô giá.
unwavering support | /ʌnˈweɪvərɪŋ səˈpɔːt/ | sự ủng hộ không lay chuyển | Her unwavering support means a lot to me. | Sự ủng hộ không đổi của mẹ rất ý nghĩa với tôi.
perseverance | /ˌpɜːsɪˈvɪərəns/ | sự kiên trì | The marathon taught me the value of perseverance. | Cuộc chạy marathon dạy tôi giá trị của sự kiên trì.
elation | /ɪˈleɪʃn/ | niềm vui sướng tột độ | I felt a sense of elation crossing the finish line. | Tôi vỡ òa vui sướng khi về đích.
butterflies in my stomach | /ˈbʌtəflaɪz ɪn maɪ ˈstʌmək/ | hồi hộp, bồn chồn | I had butterflies in my stomach before the exam. | Tôi hồi hộp trước kỳ thi.
pass with flying colors | /pɑːs wɪð ˈflaɪɪŋ ˈkʌləz/ | đỗ với kết quả xuất sắc | I'm determined to pass the exam with flying colors. | Tôi quyết tâm thi đỗ với điểm cao.
get down to business | /ɡet daʊn tə ˈbɪznəs/ | bắt tay vào việc | Right after dinner, I got down to business. | Ngay sau bữa tối, tôi bắt tay vào việc.
knuckle down | /ˈnʌkl daʊn/ | tập trung làm việc chăm chỉ | We go to the library to knuckle down on our homework. | Chúng tôi lên thư viện để tập trung làm bài.
tight deadline | /taɪt ˈdedlaɪn/ | hạn chót gấp | I feel stressed when I have tight deadlines. | Tôi căng thẳng khi có hạn chót gấp.
drained | /dreɪnd/ | kiệt sức | Before Tết, I feel completely drained. | Trước Tết tôi thấy kiệt sức.
early bird | /ˈɜːli bɜːd/ | người hay dậy sớm | I'm not naturally an early bird. | Tôi vốn không phải người hay dậy sớm.
workload | /ˈwɜːkləʊd/ | khối lượng công việc | My schedule depends on my workload. | Lịch của tôi tùy vào khối lượng công việc.

v-sp-part4.title: Speaking Part 4: cụm từ kể chuyện
v-sp-part4.body:
I'd like to talk about | /aɪd laɪk tə tɔːk əˈbaʊt/ | tôi muốn kể về | I'd like to talk about a time when I faced a challenge. | Tôi muốn kể về lần tôi đối mặt với thử thách.
at first | /ət ˈfɜːst/ | lúc đầu | At first, I felt quite worried. | Lúc đầu tôi khá lo lắng.
manage my time | /ˈmænɪdʒ maɪ taɪm/ | quản lý thời gian | I had to manage my time carefully. | Tôi phải quản lý thời gian cẩn thận.
give up | /ɡɪv ˈʌp/ | bỏ cuộc | However, I didn't give up. | Tuy nhiên, tôi không bỏ cuộc.
deal with | /ˈdiːl wɪð/ | xử lý, đối phó với | I learned how to deal with technical problems. | Tôi học được cách xử lý sự cố kỹ thuật.
overcome my fear | /ˌəʊvəˈkʌm maɪ fɪə/ | vượt qua nỗi sợ | I felt proud because I had overcome my fear. | Tôi tự hào vì đã vượt qua nỗi sợ.
step by step | /step baɪ step/ | từng bước một | We fixed the error step by step. | Chúng tôi sửa lỗi từng bước một.
relieved | /rɪˈliːvd/ | nhẹ nhõm | I was relieved because I had spent a lot of effort on it. | Tôi thấy nhẹ nhõm vì đã bỏ nhiều công sức.
proud of myself | /praʊd əv maɪˈself/ | tự hào về bản thân | I felt really happy and proud of myself. | Tôi rất vui và tự hào về bản thân.
set realistic goals | /set ˌriːəˈlɪstɪk ɡəʊlz/ | đặt mục tiêu thực tế | People should set realistic goals. | Mọi người nên đặt mục tiêu thực tế.
lifelong learning | /ˌlaɪflɒŋ ˈlɜːnɪŋ/ | học tập suốt đời | Learning is a lifelong process. | Học tập là quá trình suốt đời.
reliable source | /rɪˈlaɪəbl sɔːs/ | nguồn tin đáng tin cậy | We should check information from reliable sources. | Ta nên kiểm tra thông tin từ nguồn đáng tin cậy.
self-discipline | /ˌself ˈdɪsəplɪn/ | tính kỷ luật tự giác | Self-discipline helps me work better. | Tính tự giác giúp tôi làm việc tốt hơn.
supportive | /səˈpɔːtɪv/ | biết hỗ trợ, ủng hộ | A supportive team makes everyone more motivated. | Một đội biết hỗ trợ nhau khiến ai cũng có động lực hơn.
in my opinion | /ɪn maɪ əˈpɪnjən/ | theo tôi | In my opinion, challenges are necessary. | Theo tôi, thử thách là cần thiết.
to sum up | /tə sʌm ˈʌp/ | tóm lại | To sum up, teamwork is very important. | Tóm lại, làm việc nhóm rất quan trọng.

r2n-1.title: Sắp xếp câu: quán cà phê mới
r2n-1.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Dùng nút ↑ ↓ để sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại. Chú ý từ nối và từ thay thế (it, they, this, these).
r2n-1.body:
Last Saturday, I finally visited the new café that had opened on Bridge Street.
When I arrived, it was already full of people and the staff looked very busy.
Even so, a waiter quickly found me a small table by the window.
He handed me the menu, but I was surprised that it only had four dishes.
Since the choice was so limited, I ordered the chicken sandwich and a cup of tea.
In the end, the sandwich was delicious, so I will definitely go there again.

r2n-2.title: Sắp xếp câu: nữ ca sĩ nổi tiếng
r2n-2.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Dùng nút ↑ ↓ để sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại. Chú ý từ nối và từ thay thế (it, they, this, these).
r2n-2.body:
Mia Carter is now one of the best-known pop singers in the country.
As a teenager, she studied music and drama at a small arts school.
During those years, she often sang at school concerts and local festivals.
At these shows, she always wore colourful costumes that made her stand out.
Her unusual style and catchy songs soon attracted attention online.
Today, millions of fans follow her on social media.

r2n-3.title: Sắp xếp câu: bài tập về một đất nước
r2n-3.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Dùng nút ↑ ↓ để sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại. Chú ý từ nối và từ thay thế (it, they, this, these).
r2n-3.body:
Next week, each student will write a report about a country they have never visited.
First, choose a country and find reliable information about it.
Your research should cover its people, languages and history.
After collecting this information, compare the country with Vietnam.
In this comparison, you may discover some surprising similarities.
Finally, hand in your report to your teacher by Friday.

r2n-4.title: Sắp xếp câu: trung tâm thể thao mới
r2n-4.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Dùng nút ↑ ↓ để sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại. Chú ý từ nối và từ thay thế (it, they, this, these).
r2n-4.body:
A new sports centre opened in our town last month.
It has a large swimming pool, a gym and two tennis courts.
Because of these facilities, it quickly became popular with local families.
However, many people complained that the membership fee was too high.
In response, the manager introduced a cheaper plan for students.
Since then, the number of young members has doubled.

r3n-1.title: Ghép ý kiến: lễ hội âm nhạc
r3n-1.instr: Đọc ý kiến của 4 người. Chọn người phù hợp với mỗi câu. Một người có thể được chọn nhiều lần.
r3n-1.intro:
Tom: It was my first festival, and to be honest the first two days were a bit boring. The bands were average and it rained almost all the time, which made everything feel grey. Then on the last night my favourite band played, and that one evening made the whole trip worth it.

Hannah: I go to this festival every summer with the same group of old friends, so for me it's more about seeing them again than the music. This year the line-up was disappointing, and the camping area was a long walk from the main stage, which was tiring. I'm not sure I'll come back next year.

Daniel: I loved the mix of music – rock, jazz, electronic – there was something new every hour, and I enjoyed every single performance. The rain didn't bother me at all; dancing in the mud was part of the fun. My only complaint is the ticket price, which was far too high for students like me.

Sophie: I was there as a performer with my band, so my experience was a bit different. Playing in front of such a huge crowd was exciting, although the sound system on our stage kept breaking down. The organisers were friendly and helpful, and I'd love to be invited again.
r3n-1.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Tom | Hannah | Daniel | Sophie
Who found the first part of the festival boring? = Tom
Who thought the tickets were too expensive? = Daniel
Who goes to the festival mainly to see friends? = Hannah
Who had problems with equipment? = Sophie
Who complained about the distance between areas? = Hannah
Who did not mind the bad weather? = Daniel
Who would like to return to the festival? = Sophie

r4n-1.title: Ghép tiêu đề: phụ nữ trong khoa học
r4n-1.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
r4n-1.body:
LỰA CHỌN: A gap that starts in childhood | Different minds solve problems better | Hidden behind famous names | Prizes begin to change | Role models make a difference | Small changes in the workplace | The cost of leaving | Women now outnumber men in science
For centuries, many women contributed to scientific discoveries without receiving credit. Their work was often published under the name of a husband, brother or male supervisor, and history books remembered only the men. Researchers today are still finding letters and notebooks which show how much these women really did. = Hidden behind famous names
The imbalance seems to begin long before university. Studies show that by the age of ten, many girls already believe that science and maths are 'for boys'. Toys, books and even comments from teachers can send this message, and fewer girls then choose science subjects at secondary school. = A gap that starts in childhood
One way to change this is to make successful female scientists more visible. When schools invite women engineers or doctors to speak to their students, girls are more likely to imagine themselves in similar careers. Seeing someone 'like me' doing the job can be more powerful than any advertisement. = Role models make a difference
Even when women do enter science, many leave in the middle of their careers. Long working hours, short-term contracts and the difficulty of combining research with family life push talented people out. Each departure means that years of training and experience are lost. = The cost of leaving
Some universities and companies have introduced practical solutions, such as flexible working hours, on-site childcare and clear rules for promotion. These measures may seem minor, but they help both women and men to stay in their jobs and progress fairly. = Small changes in the workplace
Major science awards have also started to respond. For most of the twentieth century, almost every winner was a man. Now some organisations deliberately include women on their shortlists. Critics worry that this might look like 'tokenism', but supporters argue that without such steps, change would take far too long. = Prizes begin to change
Ultimately, the argument is not only about fairness. Research teams with people from different backgrounds tend to ask a wider range of questions and find more creative solutions. A more balanced scientific community is therefore likely to produce better science for everyone. = Different minds solve problems better

l3n-1.title: The Internet
l3n-1.instr: Nghe hội thoại giữa một người đàn ông và một người phụ nữ. Ai có ý kiến dưới đây: Man, Woman hay Both? Mỗi bài nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l3n-1.audio:
M: I think the internet has made us much better informed. Anyone can find the news in seconds.
W: That's true, but there's simply too much information now. I often feel overwhelmed.
M: Maybe, but you need to learn how to search properly. Finding good information is a skill.
W: I agree with that completely. Schools should teach it.
M: What worries me more is that we read so quickly online that we hardly think deeply anymore.
W: Hmm, I'm not sure. I still read long articles on my phone.
l3n-1.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
There is too much information online. = Woman
Finding good information requires skill. = Both
Reading online stops people thinking deeply. = Man
The internet keeps people better informed. = Man

l3n-2.title: University and technology
l3n-2.instr: Nghe hội thoại giữa một người đàn ông và một người phụ nữ. Ai có ý kiến dưới đây: Man, Woman hay Both? Mỗi bài nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l3n-2.audio:
W: Online lectures have been great for students. You can watch them again whenever you like.
M: Yes, I agree – being able to replay a lecture is really useful, especially before exams.
W: But I think students still need to come to campus. Meeting classmates is part of learning.
M: I'm not so sure. Lots of students make close friends online these days.
W: And another thing – universities spend too much money on new gadgets that nobody uses.
M: Well, I think that investment is necessary if they want to stay modern.
l3n-2.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Being able to replay lectures is helpful. = Both
Students should attend classes in person. = Woman
Real friendships can be formed online. = Man
Universities waste money on technology. = Woman

l3n-3.title: Politics
l3n-3.instr: Nghe hội thoại giữa một người đàn ông và một người phụ nữ. Ai có ý kiến dưới đây: Man, Woman hay Both? Mỗi bài nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l3n-3.audio:
M: I've noticed young people are much more interested in politics than they used to be.
W: Definitely. My students talk about it all the time.
M: I think social media is the main reason. They see political news every day.
W: Partly, but I think schools deserve some credit. Many now have debate clubs.
M: One thing I'd like to see is more young candidates standing for election.
W: Absolutely, that would make a real difference.
l3n-3.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Young people are becoming more interested in politics. = Both
Social media is the main cause of this change. = Man
Schools have helped to develop this interest. = Woman
More young people should stand for election. = Both

l3n-4.title: Changes in the workplace
l3n-4.instr: Nghe hội thoại giữa một người đàn ông và một người phụ nữ. Ai có ý kiến dưới đây: Man, Woman hay Both? Mỗi bài nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l3n-4.audio:
W: Working from home has completely changed how offices work.
M: It has, and I think people are actually more productive at home.
W: I'm not convinced. I find it hard to concentrate with my family around.
M: Another big change is that people don't stay in one job for life anymore.
W: That's true, and I think it's a good thing. You learn more by moving around.
M: Maybe, but companies lose a lot of experience when staff leave.
l3n-4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
People work better from home. = Man
Home can be full of distractions. = Woman
Changing jobs often is positive. = Woman
People rarely keep the same job for life now. = Both

l3n-5.title: Children and technology
l3n-5.instr: Nghe hội thoại giữa một người đàn ông và một người phụ nữ. Ai có ý kiến dưới đây: Man, Woman hay Both? Mỗi bài nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l3n-5.audio:
M: My nephew is only six, and he already has his own tablet.
W: That's very common now. I think a little screen time is fine for young children.
M: I disagree. I think it stops them from playing outside and being creative.
W: Well, some educational apps can actually help them learn to read.
M: True, some apps are well designed. But parents need to set clear limits.
W: I completely agree with you on that.
l3n-5.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Some screen time is acceptable for young children. = Woman
Tablets reduce outdoor play. = Man
Some educational apps are useful. = Both
Parents should limit screen time. = Both

l3n-6.title: Community design
l3n-6.instr: Nghe hội thoại giữa một người đàn ông và một người phụ nữ. Ai có ý kiến dưới đây: Man, Woman hay Both? Mỗi bài nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l3n-6.audio:
M: I believe the design of a neighbourhood can bring people together.
W: Maybe, but good design alone isn't enough. Building a community takes time.
M: Parks and squares give people a reason to meet, though.
W: That's true – public spaces really matter. I just think local events are even more important.
M: I'd also like to see fewer cars in residential streets.
W: I'm not sure that's realistic in a big city.
l3n-6.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Good design can help people connect. = Man
Creating a community takes time. = Woman
Public spaces are important. = Both
Streets should have less traffic. = Man

core1-g.title: Ngữ pháp: 25 câu
core1-g.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng để hoàn thành câu. Đề thật có 25 câu, mỗi câu 3 lựa chọn; một số câu là ngữ pháp văn nói (đối thoại A–B).
core1-g.body:
She has been working here ___ 2019.
*since
for
from
? Since + mốc thời gian (2019).

If I ___ more time, I would learn Japanese.
*had
have
will have
? Câu điều kiện loại 2: If + quá khứ đơn, would + V.

The report ___ by the manager yesterday.
*was written
wrote
has written
? Báo cáo không tự viết → bị động quá khứ đơn.

This is the town ___ I grew up.
*where
which
who
? where thay cho nơi chốn (in the town).

He asked me if I ___ the film before.
*had seen
have seen
see
? Câu tường thuật lùi thì → quá khứ hoàn thành.

You ___ smoke here. It's against the rules.
*mustn't
don't have to
needn't
? mustn't = bị cấm; don't have to = không cần.

I'm looking forward to ___ you next week.
*seeing
see
be seeing
? look forward to + V-ing.

By the end of this year, I ___ here for ten years.
*will have worked
will work
have worked
? "By the end of…" → tương lai hoàn thành.

A: Shall I open the window?  B: Yes, ___.
*please
I shall
you shall
? Đáp lời đề nghị giúp đỡ: Yes, please.

She suggested ___ a taxi.
*taking
to take
take
? suggest + V-ing.

I wish I ___ speak French.
*could
can
will
? wish + could: ước điều không có thật ở hiện tại.

The more you practise, the ___ you become.
*better
best
good
? The + so sánh hơn…, the + so sánh hơn.

Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.
*were
was
is
? Neither…nor: động từ theo chủ ngữ gần nhất (students → were).

I'd rather you ___ tell anyone.
*didn't
don't
won't
? would rather + S + quá khứ đơn.

It's the ___ interesting book I've ever read.
*most
more
much
? So sánh nhất đi với "I've ever…".

He's used to ___ early.
*getting up
get up
got up
? be used to + V-ing: quen với.

A: I can't swim.  B: ___ can I.
*Neither
So
Either
? Đồng ý với câu phủ định: Neither + trợ động từ + S.

They ___ dinner when the lights went out.
*were having
had
have had
? Hành động đang diễn ra (quá khứ tiếp diễn) bị hành động khác cắt ngang.

You'd better ___ a coat. It's cold.
*take
to take
taking
? had better + V nguyên mẫu.

Despite ___ tired, she finished the race.
*being
she was
to be
? Despite + V-ing / danh từ.

I haven't seen him ___ ages.
*for
since
during
? for + khoảng thời gian.

The car needs ___.
*repairing
repair
to repairing
? need + V-ing mang nghĩa bị động (cần được sửa).

A: Thanks for your help.  B: ___.
*Not at all
Yes, please
Never mind
? Not at all = không có gì.

Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
*will miss
miss
missed
? Unless = if not, điều kiện loại 1.

She's ___ a good cook that everyone loves her food.
*such
so
very
? such + a + adj + N + that.

core2-g.title: Ngữ pháp: 25 câu

core2-g.body:
I ___ to London three times.

went
was going

It's not as cold ___ yesterday.

Each of the students ___ a laptop.

have

It's time we ___ home.

go
will go
? It's time + S + quá khứ đơn.

There's ___ milk left – just enough for one cup.

a few
few
? a little + N không đếm được (còn một ít, đủ dùng).

She ___ be at home – her car is outside.
*must
can't
mustn't
? must = suy luận gần như chắc chắn.

A: I love jazz.  B: ___ do I.
*So
Neither
Too
? Đồng ý với câu khẳng định: So + trợ động từ + S.

When I arrived, the film ___.

already started
has already started
? Việc xảy ra trước một việc khác trong quá khứ → quá khứ hoàn thành.

I'm not very good ___ maths.

in
on

Although ___ rained, we went out.

it was
there

We have lived here ___ we got married.
*since
for
from

I had my hair ___ yesterday.

cutting
to cut

A: Sorry I'm late.  B: ___.

You're welcome

He ___ to work by bus, but now he drives.

uses to go

such
too

talk

will stop

most

he is

booking
book

How ___ people came to the party?

mustn't
shouldn't

A: I haven't finished yet.  B: Me ___.

too
so
? Đồng ý với câu phủ định (văn nói): Me neither.

was waiting

He apologised ___ being late.

about
of

ever

The house ___ painted at the moment.

is
has being
? Bị động tiếp diễn: is being + V3.

A: How about going to the cinema?  B: ___.

I'm going cinema

so
such

r3b2-1.intro:
Minh: I started using a language app two years ago, mainly because it was free and I could practise on the bus. It's great for building vocabulary, but I noticed that my speaking hardly improved. These days I combine it with a weekly conversation class, and that balance works well for me.

Laura: Honestly, I think apps are overrated. They turn learning into a game where you collect points, and I found myself caring more about my daily streak than about actually understanding the grammar. I eventually deleted the app and went back to traditional textbooks, which suit my learning style better.

Kevin: As a teacher, I recommend apps to my students as a supplement, never as a replacement for lessons. The best ones give instant feedback on pronunciation, which is something I can't offer thirty students at once. The danger is that learners start to believe ten minutes a day is enough.

Grace: What I love about apps is that they let me learn at my own pace. I'm quite shy, so making mistakes in front of a class used to make me anxious. With an app, nobody is watching, and I've become much more confident before I speak to real people.
r3b2-1.title: Ghép ý kiến: học ngoại ngữ bằng ứng dụng
r3b2-1.instr: Đọc ý kiến của 4 người. Chọn người phù hợp với mỗi câu. Một người có thể được chọn nhiều lần. Bài ở mức B2: chú ý các ý kiến có điều kiện và ý nói gián tiếp.
r3b2-1.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Grace | Kevin | Laura | Minh
Who believes apps can help shy learners? = Grace
Who stopped using an app completely? = Laura
Who mixes app practice with face-to-face lessons? = Minh
Who warns that short daily practice may not be enough? = Kevin
Who felt the game elements were a distraction? = Laura
Who values the instant feedback on pronunciation? = Kevin
Who says the app did not improve their speaking? = Minh

r4b2-1.title: Ghép tiêu đề: làm việc từ xa
r4b2-1.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa. Mẹo: tiêu đề thừa thường "nghe hợp lý" nhưng nói quá lên so với bài đọc.
r4b2-1.body:
LỰA CHỌN: A new map of where people live | An accidental experiment | Finding the middle ground | Gains in productivity | Managers learn to trust | Not an option for everyone | Offices disappear completely | The hidden costs of isolation
When governments around the world told people to stay at home in 2020, millions of office workers suddenly found themselves working from kitchens and bedrooms. Nobody had planned it, and few companies were prepared. Yet this unplanned situation turned into the largest experiment in working practices ever carried out, and its results are still being studied by economists, psychologists and city planners today. = An accidental experiment
One of the first surprises was that many people got more done at home. Without long commutes and constant interruptions from colleagues, employees reported that they could concentrate for longer periods. Several large surveys found that output in jobs such as programming, writing and data analysis either stayed the same or even rose, contradicting the fears of many business leaders. = Gains in productivity
However, the benefits came at a price. Many workers, especially younger ones living alone, began to feel cut off from others. Casual conversations by the coffee machine, which once seemed unimportant, turned out to play a key role in building relationships and sharing ideas. Some studies linked long periods of remote work to higher levels of loneliness and stress. = The hidden costs of isolation
The change also affected where people chose to live. Freed from the need to travel to an office every day, some families moved from expensive city centres to smaller towns or the countryside, where they could afford larger homes. Meanwhile, city-centre cafés and shops that depended on office workers saw their customers disappear almost overnight. = A new map of where people live
For managers, remote work required a new way of thinking. Instead of judging staff by how many hours they spent at their desks, they had to focus on results. This was difficult at first, and some companies introduced software to monitor employees' screens. Others, however, discovered that giving people more freedom actually increased their commitment to the company. = Managers learn to trust
It is important to remember that working from home was never possible for everyone. Nurses, shop assistants, drivers and factory workers had to continue going to their workplaces throughout the crisis. Critics point out that discussions about the 'future of work' often ignore these groups, even though they make up a large part of the workforce. = Not an option for everyone
Today, many organisations have settled on a hybrid model, in which employees spend part of the week at home and part in the office. Supporters argue that this combines the focus of home working with the creativity of face-to-face contact. Whether this compromise will last, or whether it is just one stage in a longer process of change, remains to be seen. = Finding the middle ground

l4b2-1.audio: W: Over the past five years, our city has built nearly forty kilometres of new cycle lanes. When the project began, many shop owners were strongly against it, because they feared losing parking spaces for customers. I understood their concerns. However, the latest figures show that visitors who arrive by bicycle actually visit local shops more often than drivers do, and they spend more money over a month. So, while I accept that the changes caused some disruption at first, I'm convinced the city is now a healthier and more pleasant place. The next step, I believe, should be making the lanes safer at junctions, where most accidents still happen.
l4b2-1.title: Làn đường xe đạp
l4b2-1.instr: Nghe bài nói và trả lời 2 câu hỏi về thái độ, ý kiến hoặc mục đích của người nói. Nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l4b2-1.body:
What is the speaker's opinion of the cycle lanes?
*They have benefited the city overall
They were a waste of public money
They should be removed from shopping streets
? "I'm convinced the city is now a healthier and more pleasant place."

What does the speaker think should happen next?
*Junctions should be made safer
More parking spaces should be added
Shop owners should pay for the lanes
? "The next step… should be making the lanes safer at junctions."

l4b2-2.audio: M: I went to see the film version of The Silent Harbour expecting to be disappointed, as I usually am when a favourite novel reaches the cinema. To my surprise, the director has kept the quiet, thoughtful atmosphere of the book. The acting is excellent, especially from the young lead. My only criticism is that the ending has been changed to make it happier, which removes much of the story's power. Still, I'd recommend it, though I'd advise people to read the book first so they understand what the film leaves out.
l4b2-2.title: Phim chuyển thể từ tiểu thuyết
l4b2-2.instr: Nghe bài nói và trả lời 2 câu hỏi về thái độ, ý kiến hoặc mục đích của người nói. Nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l4b2-2.body:
How did the speaker feel about the film overall?
*Pleasantly surprised
Completely disappointed
Bored by the acting
? "To my surprise, the director has kept the… atmosphere of the book." Người nói chỉ chê phần kết.

What does the speaker recommend?
*Reading the novel before watching the film
Avoiding the film altogether
Watching the film twice
? "I'd advise people to read the book first."

l4b2-3.audio: W: Every year, some students complain about group projects. They say it's unfair when one member does very little but receives the same mark as everyone else. I take this criticism seriously, and this year I've changed the system so that students also assess each other's contribution. That said, I still believe group work is essential. In almost every job, people have to cooperate with colleagues they didn't choose, and university is a safe place to learn how to do that. Learning to deal with a difficult teammate is, in my view, as valuable as the project itself.
l4b2-3.title: Làm việc nhóm ở đại học
l4b2-3.instr: Nghe bài nói và trả lời 2 câu hỏi về thái độ, ý kiến hoặc mục đích của người nói. Nghe tối đa 2 lần.
l4b2-3.body:
Why has the speaker changed the marking system?
*To respond to complaints about fairness
To reduce the amount of work for students
Because employers asked for the change
? Sinh viên phàn nàn "it's unfair…", nên giảng viên cho sinh viên chấm chéo đóng góp của nhau.

What is the speaker's main view of group work?
*It prepares students for working life
It should be made optional
It is less valuable than individual work
? "In almost every job, people have to cooperate with colleagues they didn't choose."

l4b2-4.audio: M: When the government introduced a small charge for plastic bags, many people said it would make no difference. In fact, the number of bags used fell by more than eighty percent in the first year. That's a remarkable result for such a simple measure. However, I'd warn against being too satisfied. Plastic bags were only ever a small part of the problem. Food packaging and plastic bottles are far more serious, and so far there has been little political will to tackle them. If we stop at bags, we will have missed the real opportunity.

l4b2-4.instr: Nghe bài nói và trả lời 2 câu hỏi về thái độ, ý kiến hoặc mục đích của người nói. Nghe tối đa 2 lần.

mk1-r2a.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk1-r2a.body:
Preparing well can make a big difference in a job interview.
First, find out as much as you can about the company.
This information will help you explain why you want to work there.
Next, think about the questions the interviewer is likely to ask.
Practise your answers to them aloud, ideally with a friend.
Finally, on the day itself, make sure you arrive a little early.

mk1-r2b.title: Sắp xếp câu: cuộc chạy từ thiện
mk1-r2b.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk1-r2b.body:
Last month, our office organised a charity run to raise money for the local hospital.
Over a hundred people signed up, including several of our customers.
On the morning of the race, however, it started to rain heavily.
Despite the weather, almost everyone turned up at the starting line.
Their determination paid off, as we raised more than five thousand pounds.
The hospital will use this money to buy new equipment for the children's ward.

mk1-r3.intro:
Anh: I moved from Hanoi to a small town last year to be closer to my parents. I expected to miss city life, but honestly I don't. Rent here is half what I used to pay, and I can finally afford to save. The only real problem is that good jobs are hard to find, so I still work for a city company online.

Peter: I grew up on a farm and couldn't wait to leave. For me, the city means opportunity – concerts, restaurants, people from all over the world. Yes, it's noisy and expensive, but I'd rather pay more and feel that something interesting is always happening.

Rosa: I think people romanticise the countryside. My grandparents live in a village with one bus a day, and when my grandfather got ill, the nearest hospital was an hour away. Fresh air is lovely, but access to services matters more as you get older.

Jamal: I split my time between both. During the week I work in the city, and at weekends I go to a small cottage by a lake. It gives me the best of both worlds, although the travelling is tiring and I spend a lot on petrol.
